verses.text: So King Darius gave an order, and they searched the records kept in the treasure rooms in Babylon.
A scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana in the province of Media. This is what was written in it:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, the king gave this order about God's temple in Jerusalem: Let the temple be rebuilt as a place to offer sacrifices. Let its foundations be laid firmly. It must be about twenty-seven meters high and twenty-seven meters wide.
It must have three layers of large stones and one layer of new wood. The cost will be paid from the king's treasury.

Also, the gold and silver things from God's temple, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, must be given back. Take them to the temple in Jerusalem and put each one in its place in God's temple."
Then Darius wrote: "So now, Tattenai, governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and your fellow officials west of the river, stay away from there.
Leave the work on this temple of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the Jewish leaders rebuild this temple of God on its old site.

I also order you to help these Jewish leaders build this temple of God. The full cost must be paid to these men from the king's money, from the taxes collected west of the Euphrates River, so that the work does not stop.

Whatever they need must be given to them every day without fail: young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, and wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil, as the priests in Jerusalem ask.
Then they can offer sacrifices that please the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
I also order that if anyone changes this order, a beam must be pulled from their house, and they must be lifted up and stuck on it. Their house must be made into a pile of rubble because of this.

May the God who has made his name live there destroy any king or people who tries to change this order or destroy this temple of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have given this order. Let it be done with all care."
Then Tattenai, governor of the land west of the Euphrates River, Shethar-Bozenai, and their friends did exactly what King Darius had ordered, with all care.

So the Jewish leaders kept building and did well, encouraged by the preaching of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished building the temple as the God of Israel had commanded and as Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia, had ordered.
The temple was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius's rule.
Then the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the people who had come back from being prisoners joyfully celebrated the dedication of this temple of God.

For the dedication of this temple of God they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs. As a sin offering for all Israel they offered twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
They put the priests and the Levites in their groups to serve God in Jerusalem, as written in the book of Moses.
The people who had come back from being prisoners celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

The priests and Levites had all made themselves clean together, so they were all clean. The Levites killed the Passover lambs for all the people who had come back, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

The Israelites who had come back from being prisoners ate the Passover. So did everyone who had separated themselves from the unclean ways of the nations of the land to worship the LORD, the God of Israel.

For seven days they joyfully celebrated the Festival of Bread Without Yeast. The LORD had filled them with joy by changing the heart of the king of Assyria, so that he helped them with the work on the temple of God, the God of Israel.
